doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Willcox on reading music and being the sweet trombonist
summary: Willcox says military-school overtures made him a good reader, and that he was the sweet player with a pretty tone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: As you talk I have to say something here. Now you mentioned the reading, you know, you’re a good reader, I know that when, remember I told you about Manlius Military School in that band? We’d play overtures and I got to learn how to read very well and so when my opportunity came to join, for instance the Goldkette especially, it was nothing to it. I was a good reader, so there was no question that I had a tone. You know I was the sweet guy that played the pretty stuff.
Well just pretty. I mean, I don’t mean slow music all the time, but nice tone.
